examDifficulty.heading: Is the Slack Developer Exam Hard?
examDifficulty.summary: The Slack Developer exam is moderately hard. It tests hands-on coding knowledge — Bolt framework patterns, Block Kit payloads, OAuth flows, and event handling — so reading documentation without actually building Slack apps leaves significant gaps.
bullets: 60 questions in 105 minutes — just under two minutes per question, which requires familiarity with API methods and framework patterns.
~68% passing score — you need approximately 41 correct answers out of 60 to pass, a slightly higher bar than the Slack Admin or Consultant exams.
Coding knowledge is required — questions test Bolt framework architecture, Block Kit JSON structure, OAuth scopes, and event subscription configuration.
Build before you book — candidates who have built at least one Slack app with Block Kit interactions, slash commands, and event listeners are best prepared.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Book when you have built a working Slack app using the Bolt framework with Block Kit interactions, slash commands, event subscriptions, and OAuth installation flow.

examFormat.heading: Slack Developer Exam Format Explained
examFormat.intro: The exam is proctored online or in-person. Here is the format:
examFormat.scenarioPercent: Scenario questions describe an app requirement and ask you to identify the correct API method, Block Kit layout, event subscription, or OAuth scope to implement it.
bestWayToPass: Bolt framework: Know app initialization, event listeners, action handlers, and the OAuth 2.0 installation flow for multi-workspace app distribution.
Block Kit: Study block types (section, actions, input, context) and element types (button, static_select, datepicker, plain_text_input) and their JSON payload structure.
Events and commands: Understand the 3-second acknowledgement rule, event subscription configuration, and how to handle slash command and interaction payloads.
Security best practices: Master request signature verification (HMAC-SHA256), secure token storage, and the principle of least-privilege when requesting OAuth scopes.

certificationCard.description: This exam tests building custom Slack apps using the Bolt framework, Block Kit UI components, Events API, slash commands, and OAuth-based app distribution across workspaces.

keyConcepts.h2: Slack Developer: Key Concepts for the Exam

blocks.heading: Slack API: Bolt Framework and Authentication
blocks.body: The Bolt framework (available for Node.js, Python, Java) simplifies Slack app development by handling **OAuth**, event dispatching, and middleware. App authentication: Bot token (scoped to workspace, long-lived) vs User token (acts on behalf of a specific user). OAuth 2.0 installation flow for distributing apps to other workspaces. Socket Mode enables the app to receive events without a public HTTP endpoint — useful for development and firewalled environments. HTTP mode requires a public URL and event subscription verification.

blocks.heading: Slack Surfaces: Home Tab, Messages, and Modals
blocks.body: Home Tab: a persistent, personalised app canvas shown when the user clicks the app in the sidebar — updated via views.publish API. Messages: posted in channels or DMs — can include Block Kit UI elements (buttons, select menus, input fields) for interactivity. Modals: triggered by button clicks or slash commands — multi-step forms with view.push/update/open. Each surface has different use cases: Home Tab for dashboards, Messages for notifications with actions, Modals for data entry. The exam tests which surface to use for a given app interaction pattern.

blocks.heading: Block Kit: Interactive UI Components
blocks.body: Block Kit is Slack's UI framework. Block types: Section (text + accessory), Actions (buttons, select menus), Input (form fields), Context (supporting text/images), Header (bold title), Divider. Elements: button (click actions), static_select (dropdown), datepicker, plain_text_input. Block Kit Builder (online tool) lets developers compose and preview UI. Interactivity payloads (block_actions for button clicks, view_submission for modal forms) are sent to the app's interaction endpoint. The exam tests composing Block Kit payloads for common app UIs.

blocks.heading: Events API and Slash Commands
blocks.body: Events API delivers workspace events (messages posted, users joining, reactions added) to the app's endpoint. Subscribe to specific event types to minimise payload volume. 3-second response requirement: acknowledge the event with HTTP 200 immediately, process asynchronously if the task takes longer. Slash Commands provide custom commands (/myapp action) — configured in app settings, delivered as HTTP POST to the command endpoint. The exam tests how to subscribe to the correct events and how to handle slash command payloads.

blocks.heading: Security: Token Management and Signature Verification
blocks.body: Never expose bot tokens in client-side code or version control. Store tokens in environment variables or secrets management systems. Slack signs all inbound payloads with a signing secret — verify the X-Slack-Signature header using HMAC-SHA256 to prevent spoofed requests. Token rotation: **OAuth** tokens can be rotated programmatically. App scopes should follow least privilege — request only the OAuth scopes the app actually needs. The exam tests signature verification implementation and token security best practices.

scenarioTips.h2: How to Pass the Salesforce Slack Developer Exam
scenarioTips.intro: The Slack Developer exam tests technical development skills for building Slack apps. Focus on the Slack API, Bolt framework, event handling, and building interactive workflows using Block Kit.

blocks.heading: Bolt Framework Architecture
blocks.body: Know how to build Slack apps using the Bolt framework (Node.js, Python, Java): app initialization, event handling, action handling, shortcut handling, and how **OAuth** 2.0 app installation works.

blocks.heading: Block Kit UI Framework
blocks.body: Know how to build rich interactive messages using Block Kit: block types (section, actions, input, context), element types (button, select, date picker, text input), and how to use Block Kit Builder for prototyping.

blocks.heading: Event API & Interactivity
blocks.body: Know how Slack's Event API delivers events to your app (message events, reaction events, app_mention), how to configure event subscriptions, and how to respond to interactive components (modals, actions).

blocks.heading: Workflow Steps
blocks.body: Know how to build custom Workflow Steps using the workflow_step_edit and workflow_step_execute events. Understand how to create the configuration modal and process step execution callbacks.

blocks.heading: App Distribution & Security
blocks.body: Know how to distribute Slack apps through the Slack App Directory, implement scoped **OAuth** for multi-workspace apps, and security best practices: token storage, request signature verification, and HTTPS requirements.

sampleQuestions.question: Which Slack API is used to build interactive components like buttons and menus?
options: REST API only
Block Kit
Web API
Events API only
sampleQuestions.explanation: Block Kit is the UI framework for designing interactive message surfaces in Slack apps.
whyWrong: The REST API is the general term; Block Kit is the specific framework for interactive UI elements.
The Web API is used to call methods generally, not specifically for interactive component layout.
The Events API delivers event notifications, not the UI building blocks for buttons and menus.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the purpose of Slack App Manifests?
options: To deploy to Heroku
To define app configuration in YAML
To send emails
To configure CPQ
sampleQuestions.explanation: App Manifests allow you to define Slack app configuration (scopes, events, shortcuts) in YAML.
whyWrong: Deploying to Heroku is a hosting decision, unrelated to what a manifest defines.
Sending emails is unrelated to app configuration.
CPQ configuration is unrelated to Slack app manifests.

sampleQuestions.question: Which Slack event type is fired when a user joins a channel?
options: message
member_joined_channel
app_mention
reaction_added
sampleQuestions.explanation: member_joined_channel is the event emitted when a user joins a public or private channel.
whyWrong: 'message' fires for message events, not channel joins.
app_mention fires when the app is @-mentioned, not on channel joins.
reaction_added fires for emoji reactions, not channel joins.

sampleQuestions.question: What does the Slack Web API method chat.postMessage do?
options: Delete a message
Post a message to a channel
Create a channel
List users
sampleQuestions.explanation: chat.postMessage sends a message to a channel, user DM, or other conversation.
whyWrong: chat.postMessage doesn't delete messages — chat.delete handles that.
Creating a channel uses a different method (conversations.create).
Listing users uses a different method (users.list) — chat.postMessage only posts messages.

sampleQuestions.question: Which OAuth scope is required to post messages as your app?
options: users:read
chat:write
channels:history
im:read
sampleQuestions.explanation: chat:write allows the app to post messages to channels and conversations.
whyWrong: users:read grants profile visibility, not messaging permission.
channels:history grants read access to message history, not posting rights.
im:read grants read access to direct messages, not the ability to post as the app.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the Bolt Framework in Slack app development?
options: A deployment pipeline for Slack apps
Slack's official framework for building apps in JavaScript, Python, and Java with built-in handlers for events, actions, and shortcuts
A database management tool for Slack data
A UI design kit for Block Kit layouts
sampleQuestions.explanation: Bolt abstracts Slack API complexity, providing a framework with built-in handling for events, actions, shortcuts, and commands.
whyWrong: Bolt isn't a deployment pipeline — it's an application framework.
Bolt doesn't manage Slack data storage — that's outside its scope.
Bolt is a code framework, not a visual UI design kit.

sampleQuestions.question: How do you register and handle a slash command in a Slack app?
options: Define it in the app's package.json file
Register it in the App Manifest or App Settings under Slash Commands, then handle the incoming POST payload in your app server
Add it directly to a Block Kit message surface
Use only the Slack Web API chat.postMessage method
sampleQuestions.explanation: Slash commands are registered in App Settings (or App Manifest), and your server must respond to the incoming POST payload within 3 seconds.
whyWrong: package.json configures npm dependencies, not Slack slash command registration.
Slash commands aren't defined inside Block Kit messages — they're a separate app configuration.
chat.postMessage sends messages; it doesn't register a slash command.

sampleQuestions.question: What Slack API method is used to open a modal in response to a user interaction?
options: chat.postMessage
views.open
conversations.open
users.info
sampleQuestions.explanation: views.open opens a modal dialog using a trigger_id obtained from an interaction payload. The modal must be opened within 3 seconds of the trigger.
whyWrong: chat.postMessage posts a message, not a modal.
conversations.open opens a DM/group conversation, not a modal dialog.
users.info retrieves user profile data — it doesn't open UI surfaces.

sampleQuestions.question: What is Socket Mode in Slack apps and when should you use it?
options: A real-time database sync method for Slack data
A connection method that delivers event payloads over a WebSocket, allowing apps to receive events without exposing a public HTTP endpoint
An OAuth token type for machine-to-machine apps
A Block Kit interactive element type
sampleQuestions.explanation: Socket Mode is ideal for development or firewalled environments — it eliminates the need for a publicly accessible HTTPS endpoint to receive events.
whyWrong: Socket Mode is unrelated to database synchronization.
Socket Mode isn't a token type — it's a connection method.
Socket Mode is a connection mechanism, not a Block Kit UI element.

sampleQuestions.question: What is an Incoming Webhook in Slack?
options: A method for receiving messages sent to your app from Slack users
A simple URL that accepts HTTP POST requests to post messages to a specific Slack channel, without needing a full app installation
A Block Kit element for embedding external content
An event fired when a webhook URL is triggered from outside Slack
sampleQuestions.explanation: Incoming Webhooks provide a pre-configured URL that accepts HTTP POST requests to post messages to a channel — useful for notifications from external systems.
whyWrong: Incoming Webhooks send messages out, they don't receive messages from users.
Incoming Webhooks aren't a Block Kit element — they're a separate posting mechanism.
This describes an outbound trigger you configure, not an event fired externally.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the difference between a Global Shortcut and a Message Shortcut in Slack?
options: They are identical in functionality and scope
Global Shortcuts are accessible from the shortcut menu anywhere in Slack; Message Shortcuts appear in the context menu of a specific message
Message Shortcuts require workspace admin approval before use
Global Shortcuts only work in direct messages, not channels
sampleQuestions.explanation: Global Shortcuts launch from the lightning bolt icon anywhere in Slack; Message Shortcuts appear when right-clicking a specific message.
whyWrong: They differ meaningfully — Global and Message Shortcuts have different access points.
There's no admin-approval distinction between the two shortcut types by default.
Global Shortcuts aren't restricted to DMs only — they're accessible more broadly.

sampleQuestions.question: How does Slack enforce API rate limits and what happens when they are exceeded?
options: There are no rate limits — all methods are unlimited
Methods have tiered rate limits per minute per workspace (Tier 1–4). Exceeding limits returns HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header indicating when to retry
All methods share a single fixed limit of 100 requests per hour
Rate limits only apply to Incoming Webhooks, not Web API methods
sampleQuestions.explanation: Slack Web API methods have tiered rate limits (Tier 1–4). The 429 response includes a Retry-After header — apps must back off and retry after the specified delay.
whyWrong: Slack does enforce rate limits — 'unlimited' is incorrect.
Rate limits vary by tier (1–4), not a single fixed number.
Rate limits apply broadly across Web API methods, not just Incoming Webhooks.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the App Home tab in a Slack app?
options: A Slack channel automatically created for app notifications
A dedicated, persistent space where an app displays a customised view for each user, built with Block Kit via views.publish
The app's settings page in the Slack App Directory
A tab for managing the app's channel memberships
sampleQuestions.explanation: The App Home tab provides each user a private, personalised space. Your app controls the content by calling views.publish with the user ID and Block Kit layout.
whyWrong: App Home isn't an auto-created notification channel — it's a dedicated per-user view.
App Home is a feature within the app experience, not the App Directory settings page.
App Home isn't specifically about channel membership management.

sampleQuestions.question: How must a Slack app respond to an interactive component action such as a button click?
options: Send a new message to the channel immediately
Acknowledge the action within 3 seconds with HTTP 200, then perform any async processing and update the message or open a modal
Call chat.delete to remove the original message containing the button
Reply in the message thread only, without acknowledging the payload
sampleQuestions.explanation: Slack requires acknowledgement within 3 seconds to avoid showing a timeout error to the user. Use ack() or respond() first, then process asynchronously.
whyWrong: Sending a new message doesn't satisfy the required immediate acknowledgment step.
Deleting the original message doesn't fulfill Slack's required acknowledgment protocol.
Replying in a thread doesn't substitute for the required HTTP 200 acknowledgment within 3 seconds.

sampleQuestions.question: Which Slack API delivers event notifications to your app when subscribed events occur in a workspace?
options: Web API
Events API
Block Kit API
SCIM Provisioning API
sampleQuestions.explanation: The Events API sends event payloads to your app's endpoint (or Socket Mode connection) whenever a subscribed event fires — message posted, reaction added, member joined, etc.
whyWrong: The Web API is used to call methods, not to receive push notifications about events.
Block Kit defines UI layout, not event delivery.
SCIM Provisioning API manages user provisioning, unrelated to event notifications.
